events.title: Karl Benz is born
events.description: German engineer Karl Benz was born on this day. He grew up to build one of the first practical automobiles powered by an internal combustion engine.
events.significance: His 1886 Benz Patent-Motorwagen is widely regarded as the first true production automobile. It helped launch the age of personal motorized transport.

events.title: Germany and Japan sign the Anti-Comintern Pact
events.description: Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan signed an agreement that was officially aimed at opposing the Communist International. It also marked growing cooperation between the two powers.
events.significance: The pact was an early step toward the Axis alliance of World War II. Italy joined it in 1937.

events.title: The Mousetrap opens in London's West End
events.description: Agatha Christie's murder mystery The Mousetrap had its opening night in London. It went on to become one of the most famous plays in theatre history.
events.significance: It became the longest continuously running play in the world, and its closing twist is famously kept secret by audiences.

events.title: The Mirabal sisters are murdered in the Dominican Republic
events.description: Patria, Minerva and María Teresa Mirabal were activists who opposed the dictatorship of Rafael Trujillo. They were killed, and their deaths were staged to look like an accident.
events.significance: Their killing helped fuel the movement that ended Trujillo's rule. In 1999 the United Nations designated November 25 as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

events.title: Military coup ousts Greek President Papadopoulos
events.description: Greece's army removed President George Papadopoulos from power. This came about a week after the government violently suppressed student-led protests at the Athens Polytechnic.
events.significance: The coup replaced one military regime with a harsher one. That regime collapsed in 1974, and Greece returned to democracy.
